name: Northern Irish Ulster Fry
description: The Ulster fry is genuinely defined by what separates it from a full Irish or full English breakfast - real soda farl and potato farl, both griddle-cooked rather than oven-baked, are what make it specifically Northern Irish, not just eggs, bacon, and sausage together.
steps_detailed: Fry the sausage, 8-9 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Warm the bacon and tomatoes in the same pan.
Fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve everything together on one plate, alongside soda farl and potato farl - real Ulster fry is defined by including both.

name: Northern Irish Soda Farl
description: Soda farl, a quick griddle bread, genuinely gets its name from the Scottish word 'fardel', meaning a fourth part - real technique rolls the dough into a round and cuts it into quarters before cooking, and critically, it's cooked on a dry griddle or skillet, never baked in the oven like standard soda bread.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, baking soda, and salt, then stir in the milk until just combined into a soft dough - real technique avoids overworking it.
Pat into a round about half an inch thick and cut into quarters.
Cook on a dry, hot skillet or griddle, 6-8 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through - real soda farl is never baked in the oven.

name: Northern Irish Potato Farl
description: Potato farl, traditionally made from leftover mashed potato, is the other real defining bread of the Ulster fry - real technique mixes cold mashed potato with flour and butter into a workable dough, cut into quarters and griddle-cooked until golden.
steps_detailed: Mix the cold mashed potato with the flour and melted butter into a soft, workable dough.
Roll to about half an inch thick and cut into quarters.
Cook on a hot, lightly oiled griddle, 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown outside and soft within.

name: Northern Irish Champ
description: Champ, mashed potato worked with real chopped scallions and a generous well of melted butter in the center, is a beloved Northern Irish side, real technique making a real butter well at the table rather than mixing it all in.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw

ingredients.ingredient: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw

steps_detailed: Cook the scallions briefly in the milk, 2 minutes, then mash into the potato.
Serve with a generous well of the butter melting in the center - real tradition eats from the outside in, dipping each bite into the butter well.

name: Northern Irish Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Northern Irish home cooking.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Northern Irish Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with butter and lemon, reflecting Northern Ireland's rich Atlantic and Irish Sea coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the butter and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Northern Irish Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Northern Ireland.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.
